meta.title: Friends with Habits — Habit Tracker with an Accountability Partner
meta.description: A free habit tracker built around accountability partners. Make a pact with a friend, check in daily with photo proof, and keep each other on streak.
meta.ogImageAlt: Friends with Habits — habits that stick when a friend's on the hook too.

hero.motto: Friends don't let friends give up on change.
hero.headlineHtml: Habits that stick when a friend's on the hook too.

popular.heading: Bring the challenge you're already doing.
popular.intro: Step goals, zone 2, cold showers, the two-minute rule. The habits everyone is talking about are better with someone on the other end. Pick one, invite the friend who's doing it too, and run it for 7 to 90 days.
popular.pactsAriaLabel: Ready-made pacts you can start today
popular.note: All of these are ready-made in the app, alongside more than 40 others. Or write your own.

steps.heading: Three steps. Two people. One streak.
steps.intro: A pact takes a minute to set up and a friend to keep. Everything else is just showing up.
steps.createBody: Pick a habit — workout, reading, meditation, anything daily. Set the time you'll both show up.
steps.inviteBody: Send them a link. Your friend joins and becomes your accountability partner — the person who notices if you stop.
steps.checkInBody: Add a photo or quick note as proof. Watch the streak grow together.

noFriend.heading: None of your friends on the app yet? Start anyway.
noFriend.bodyHtml: Your first habit can run solo for a week with no invite at all. Send one invite whenever you are ready — by text, to anyone — and you can keep checking in whether or not they have accepted yet. The pact starts the day they join.
noFriend.challengeHtml: Or turn it into a challenge: share one link, and anyone can join the board and check in from the web without installing the app.

why.heading: Why a partner makes the difference
why.intro: Committing out loud, to a person, by a set time, is one of the oldest tricks for following through. The two figures below are the ones you will see quoted everywhere; read them as the shape of the gap, not as a measurement.
why.withPartnerHtml: With an accountability appointment. The often-quoted follow-through rate for a goal when you have a set time to report back to the person you committed to.
why.onYourOwnHtml: As an idea. The often-quoted rate for the same goal when it stays an idea you never commit to anyone. Solo apps leave you on this side of the gap; we make the other side the default.
why.sourceNoteHtml: These figures are widely attributed to the American Society for Training & Development (now ATD), but we have not been able to trace them to a published study, so treat them as illustrative. They are not measurements of this app's users. Smaller published work points the same way: in a 2015 study by Gail Matthews at Dominican University of California, people who sent weekly progress reports to a friend accomplished significantly more of their goals than people who kept their goals to themselves.

compare.heading: How it's different from other habit trackers
compare.partnerRequiredHtml: A partner is required, not optional. Streaks, Habitify, Done and most other habit apps are built for one person. Here a pact needs two, so there is no version of the app where nobody notices you stopped.
compare.proofHtml: Check-ins carry proof. Every daily check-in takes a photo or a note, so a streak is evidence rather than a tap.
compare.sharedStreakHtml: The streak is shared. You and your partner are on the same streak, so a missed day costs both of you — the reason it is uncomfortable is the reason it works.
compare.freeHtml: It is free to start. No invite code, no card. Install it on Android, or sign in from any browser to check in.
compare.noSubscriptionHtml: No subscription to sign up for. Free accounts track up to {freeHabitLimit} active habits at a time, free for as long as you use it. If you want more, the first 5,000 accounts can lift that limit permanently with a one-time $20 founder unlock instead of a monthly bill.

whatIs.question: What is Friends with Habits?
whatIs.answer: Friends with Habits is a habit-tracking app that requires an accountability partner. Instead of tracking a habit alone, you make a pact with a friend: you both commit to the same daily habit, you both check in with proof, and you both see it when the other one misses.

isFree.question: Is Friends with Habits free?
isFree.answer: Yes. Friends with Habits is free to download and free to use, with no invite code and no card. A free account tracks up to {freeHabitLimit} active habits at a time, with no expiry, and archiving a habit you have finished with frees its slot. Free accounts can also start a limited number of new habits each month. The optional $20 founder unlock lifts both limits.

founderUnlock.question: What is the $20 founder unlock, and do I need it?
founderUnlock.answer: You do not need it: the free tier is free for as long as you use it, with up to {freeHabitLimit} active habits at a time. The founder unlock is for people who want more. The first 5,000 accounts can pay $20 once and never pay again; it removes the free tier's habit limits and includes every premium feature we add later, for life. There is no subscription attached to it and nothing to cancel. You buy it inside the app through Google Play, and once 5,000 people have claimed it the offer is gone for good.

whatIsPact.question: What is a pact?
whatIsPact.answer: A pact is a daily habit that you and a friend commit to together — a workout, a reading session, a meditation, a language lesson, anything you want to do every day. The pact holds the habit, the schedule, and the streak that the two of you share.

needFriend.question: Do I need a friend to use the app?
needFriend.answer: Not to get started. Your first habit can run solo for a week without inviting anyone, and after that you keep checking in as soon as you have sent a single invite, whether or not your friend has accepted yet. Pacts are still the point: a pact needs two people, because solo habit trackers let you quit in private, which is the failure mode this app exists to remove. If your friend has not installed the app yet, your invite link walks them through it.

checkIns.question: How do daily check-ins work?
checkIns.answer: Each day you check in on your pact and attach a photo or a short note as proof. Your partner sees the check-in, you see theirs, and the shared streak grows for every day you both show up. Miss a day and the streak resets for both of you.

iphone.question: Is Friends with Habits available on iPhone?
iphone.answer: There is no iPhone app yet, but you do not need one to take part. Create an account and sign in at habits.therr.com on your iPhone to see your habits, check in each day and ask to join open pacts, all from the browser. The Android app is on Google Play, an iOS app is next on the roadmap, and the same account works on all of them.
